**Observations:**
- **Plant part affected**: Stem/crown area at or just below the soil line; stem has been split open to show internal tissue
- **External**: White/grayish mycelial mat visible on the outer stem surface at the crown
- **Internal**: Bleached, white-to-yellow internal stem tissue, with decay progressing inward
- **Plant condition**: Completely wilted and dead; leaves brown and desiccated
- **Soil type**: Sandy soil, visible around the crown
- **Environment**: Consistent with warm, well-drained conditions

**Reasoning through candidate diseases:**

- **Southern Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*): Crown/stem rot at soil line with white mycelial mat on stem surface; small sclerotia (sometimes visible); thrives in hot, sandy conditions. Matches well.
- **Sclerotinia Timber Rot** (*Sclerotinia sclerotiorum*): Also produces white cottony mycelium and stem rot, but internal large black sclerotia are diagnostic — not clearly visible here. Prefers cooler, moister conditions than this sandy scene.
- **Verticillium Wilt**: Would show brown vascular streaking inside stem, no external mycelium.
- **Phytophthora Blight**: Water-soaked, dark brown/black lesions, not white mycelium.
- **Bacterial Wilt variants**: No fungal mycelium expected.

The key discriminating features — **white mycelial mat on the stem at the soil line**, **crown rot**, **complete plant wilt**, and **sandy soil** — are classic for Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*).
